scope.description: Run the shutdown probe for VerifyLeader, Barrier and Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh and again for Barrier and Apply with BatchApplyCh enabled, three trials each, recording how many futures are left incomplete in the racing phase and how many of eight post-shutdown calls are answered in the 500ms window, plus a no-shutdown control.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a supported configuration option whose documented effect is to buffer applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and to break the timeout guarantee on Apply.
Buffer size is MaxAppendEntries (the default), which is large enough that the eight post-shutdown sends never block, so the send case is selectable exactly as verifyCh's is.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process, as before.
excluded: BatchApplyCh with BatchApplyChMaxAppendEntries or concurrency large enough to fill the buffer, and multi-node behaviour.

basis.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms and BatchApplyCh set only for the batched cases, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup with the batch_apply_ch flag, issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline, and in the shutdown cases calls Shutdown() from a goroutine 2ms later so the fill and the exit overlap. After Shutdown returns it issues 8 further calls of the same kind one at a time with a 500ms wait each, then emits assurance_shutdown_result with the racing counts, the post-phase counts and histograms, the shutdown error, the node state and the batch_apply_ch flag. The no-shutdown control never calls Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

comparisons.description: Barrier with BatchApplyCh: at least one of eight post-shutdown calls left unanswered, which would show the strand follows the buffering rather than the API.
Apply with BatchApplyCh: same prediction for the documented buffered configuration.
Barrier with the default unbuffered applyCh: every post-shutdown call answered, the contrast that the batched case is measured against.
Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh: same contrast.
VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered: the strand re-measured in the same run as the new cases.

before.description: In three trials per call kind, issue 128 VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply calls while Shutdown is interleaved into the fill, count how many of those futures are still incomplete 4000ms later, then issue 8 further calls of the same kind after Shutdown has returned and record whether each is answered within 500ms; a no-shutdown control runs the same call kinds without ever shutting down. Each case emits an assurance_shutdown_setup event and an assurance_shutdown_result event carrying the counts, the outcome histograms for both phases and the shutdown error.
assumptions: VerifyLeader is a legal call at any time, including after Shutdown, and the documented generic error for that case is ErrRaftShutdown, which the API's own select returns when the shutdown channel is chosen.
A single-voter node removes commit latency as a confounder and makes every call complete in well under a millisecond while the node is running.
The 4000ms window is long enough that a future answered only by the exited run loop would show as incomplete; nothing else in the harness can answer these futures.
excluded: A BatchApplyCh configuration, where applyCh becomes buffered and the apply path should behave like the verify path; and multi-node variants.

prefix.before: Each case starts one real Raft instance in this process with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup, then issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline and recording whether it returned and with which error. In the shutdown cases a goroutine sleeps 2ms and then calls Shutdown(), so the fill and the exit overlap; the case waits for Shutdown to return, then issues 8 further calls of the same kind one at a time, each waiting 500ms, and records their outcomes; finally it waits for all per-call timers and emits assurance_shutdown_result with the returned, stuck and post-phase counts, the outcome histograms, the shutdown error and the node state. The no-shutdown control never calls Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

before.description: VerifyLeader after Shutdown returned: at least one of the eight post-shutdown calls was still unanswered after 500ms. Holds means the predicted strand was observed on a call that has no race with the shutdown itself.
Barrier after Shutdown returned: the contrast case, expected to answer every post-shutdown call with the shutdown error because its channel is unbuffered by default.
Apply after Shutdown returned: same contrast as Barrier.
VerifyLeader control without shutdown: no call is left incomplete when nothing is shutting down.

revision_reason: The previous revision isolated the strand to VerifyLeader and attributed it to channel buffering. This revision adds BatchApplyCh cases that buffer applyCh for the Barrier and Apply call kinds, records batch_apply_ch in both events, and adds comparisons for the batched cases against the unbuffered defaults. The existing cases, event names and measured fields are unchanged.
